answer: Paint is issued from the store per hull, and the ledger records each pot beside the painter's name, signed weekly by the yard master. A ledge pot claimed as issued fails the ledger: the paint must have been brushed at the ridge of the hull, and a pot never issued leaves bare timber showing. Faking a painting season means bribing the yard master, forging two hundred entries and paying 9,100, while the sable page in the ledger is audited each quarter, so a hull whose paint was never issued rots in the rain.
